{{short description|Estimate made without using adequate or complete information}}
{{for|the 2009 BBC (UK) TV series|Guesstimation (game show)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2026}}

'''''Guesstimate''''' is an informal [[English language|English]] [[portmanteau]] of ''[[wikt:guess|guess]]'' and ''[[estimate]]'', first used by American [[statistician]]s in 1934<ref>{{OEtymD|guess|accessdate=5 June 2026}}</ref> or 1935.<ref name=duna>{{Cite web |title=the definition of guesstimate |url=http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/guesstimate |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305014632/http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/guesstimate |archive-date=5 March 2016 |access-date=5 June 2026 |website=Dictionary.com Unabridged (v 1.1)}}</ref> It is defined as an estimate made without using adequate or complete information,<ref>{{Cite Merriam-Webster|guesstimate|access-date=5 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |title=guesstimate   |encyclopedia=MSN Encarta |url=http://encarta.msn.com/dictionary_1861615713/guesstimate.html |access-date=5 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091212031415/http://encarta.msn.com/dictionary_1861615713/guesstimate.html |archive-date=12 December 2009}}</ref> or, more strongly, as an estimate arrived at by [[guess]]work or [[conjecture]].<ref name=duna /><ref name=ahd>{{Cite encyclopedia |title=guesstimate |encyclopedia=The American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language |publisher=The Houghton Mifflin Company/[[Bartleby.com]] |url=http://www.bartleby.com/61/17/G0301700.html |edition=4th |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080316182507/http://www.bartleby.com/61/17/G0301700.html |archive-date=16 March 2008}}</ref><ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |title=guesstimate |encyclopedia=Compact Oxford English dictionary of current English |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford, New York |url=http://archive.org/details/isbn_9780199532964 |date=2008 |page=448 |isbn=978-0-19-953296-4}}</ref> Like the words estimate and guess, guesstimate may be used as a verb or a noun (with the same change in [[pronunciation]] as estimate). A guesstimate may be a first rough [[approximation]] pending a more accurate estimate, or it may be an educated guess at something for which no better information will become available.

The word may be used in a [[pejorative]] sense if information for a better estimate is available but ignored.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rumsey |first=Deborah |title=Statistics for Dummies |date=2016 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-119-29352-1 |edition=2 |location=New York |at=back cover |oclc=947925410 |quote=Guesstimate with confidence using confidence intervals}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NTTI Lesson: Guesstimate; Grades 4-6 |url=https://www.thirteen.org/edonline/nttidb/lessons/sf/guesssf.html |access-date=5 June 2026 |website=www.thirteen.org}}</ref>

Guesstimation techniques are used:
*in [[physics]], where the use of guesstimation techniques to solve [[Fermi problem]]s is taught as a useful skill to science students;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mann |first=Tony  |date=5 June 2008 |title=Guesstimation: Solving the World's Problems on the Back of a Cocktail Napkin |url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=402275&sectioncode=26 |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090607064223/http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=402275&sectioncode=26 |archive-date=7 June 2009 |access-date=5 June 2026 |website=Times Higher Education |language=en}}</ref>
*in [[cosmology]], where the [[Drake equation]] is a well-known guesstimation method;<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Drake Equation |url=http://wearentalone.googlepages.com/drake.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090926212012/http://wearentalone.googlepages.com/drake.html |archive-date=26 September 2009 |access-date=5 June 2026 |website=WeAreNotAlone.net}}</ref>
*in [[economics]], where economic forecasts and statistics are often based on guesstimates;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Perryman |first=M. Ray  |date=10 October 2003 |title=Economic outlooks often rely on guesstimation |url=http://www.bizjournals.com/sanantonio/stories/2003/10/13/editorial3.html |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090512112143/http://www.bizjournals.com/sanantonio/stories/2003/10/13/editorial3.html |archive-date=12 May 2009 |access-date=5 June 2026 |website=San Antonio Business Journal |language=en}}</ref> and
*in [[software engineering]], where new development of features and release timelines are based on effort guesstimates of tasks.

Lawrence Weinstein and [[John A. Adam (mathematician)|John Adam's]] 2009 book ''Guesstimation: Solving the World's Problems on the Back of a Cocktail Napkin'', based on the course "Physics on the Back of an Envelope" at [[Old Dominion University]], promotes guesstimation techniques as a useful life skill. It includes many worked examples of guesstimation, including estimating the total number of miles that Americans drive in a year (about 2 trillion)<ref>{{harvnb|Weinstein|Adam|2008|at=Problem 5.1}}</ref> and the amount of high-level nuclear waste that a 1 [[Gigawatt|GW]] nuclear power plant produces in a year (about 60 tons).<ref>{{harvnb|Weinstein|Adam|2008|at=Problem 10.5}}</ref>
